item.description: Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · post Sharing some more UI previews for Superlogical, this time the "tab peek." If you three-finger swipe down, you can "peek" at the other session tabs. These are live-updating, metal-rendered previews including splits. If ...
item.content:encoded:
Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · post

Sharing some more UI previews for Superlogical, this time the "tab peek." If you three-finger swipe down, you can "peek" at the other session tabs. These are live-updating, metal-rendered previews including splits. If you keep dragging, you enter a "mission control" style mode.


This is one of those UI patterns that once you get used to, you mindlessly find yourself doing it ALL THE TIME. It's a great way to quickly take a look at everything thats going on. You aren't reading the mini text of course, but the shape of it tells you a lot about where things are.


The peek pushes the terminal down off screen, it doesn't resize it, so it doesn't force any weird reflow or anything either.


There's a lot more to talk about, especially about how this interacts with how we expose what needs attention so you can easily find the terminals/sessions/etc. that require your attention.


Of course, you'll be able to drive this with the keyboard too. :)


As always, a disclaimer: this is all early work subject to change, just trying to share some of what we're building in public. A lot of the UI experiential design is

@almonk

so follow him for more updates too!

NatSock (@mynatsockacct) · context

waaahhh i can't remember what my sessions do without 4 minutes of animated cutscenes applied to my tabs

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

We respect the macOS settings to limit animation (we disable it).

paperbenni (@paperbenni) · context

I thought this was supposed to be a multiplexer? That looks like fancy ghostty. Can I close the window and the sessions keep active?

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

The best multiplexer in the world is going to be the one that makes you forget it exists. Everything you see here is a remote terminal. The little icon to the left of the tabs is a list of sessions. When you restart it restores. You can join from another comptuer. You can even join from your phone.

Brendon Ghaderi (@br3ndong) · context

Is this available for public use? Would love to help beta test

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

Not yet

vogel (@ryanvogel) · context

is it only gonna be Mac

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

No, but the clients will be unapologetically designed for their platforms. Not every OS will support the same UI features. We want people to think it’s not cross platform cause it’s so damn good on each.


Beta will be web plus Apple (macOS iOS) only for GUI. Server runs on Linux too but native GUI there to start. Windows we’re hiring for.

roman (@nulladdict) · context

any chance this will get rid of the native macos tabs that conflict with macos tiling managers?

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

Yes, that's fixed because this is a fully custom tab bar.

Arihant (@arihantbansal) · context

will the peek UI be updating real time? so I can see if agents have stopped working in another tab vs still ongoing?

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

Yes it does and you can already see it in this video

nkxxll (@nkxxll) · context

love this <3 only thing I am missing are sessions. I find myself working on at least two projects at a time all the time and I want that all in one window.

are there plans to make this session view better ;) (herdr btw.):

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

That little icon next to the tabs are sessions.

item.content:encoded:
Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · post

We're looking to hire Windows developers capable of producing UI at this quality (but, idiomatic to the Windows ecosystem, not cloning Apple). If you are one or know someone, please have them apply via `ssh

http://

superlogical.jobs`. We've been struggling to find this person.


There's just a lot of Windows applications out there (like, almost all of them) that just aren't good. We're looking for someone who wants to create a Windows applications that sparks joy, excites people, and feels good. We want frame perfect animation. We want obsessive consideration over user flows, click counts, keyboard press counts, etc.


We're a team that has that kind of obsession, but lacks the Windows experience. If you know a Windows dev who has this quality obsession and wants to work with a group that shares those ideals, I want to talk to them.

Gordon Cassie (@gordon_cassie) · context

I sent someone great your way but he hasn't heard anything.

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

I thought we reached out, let me double check. Sorry about that.

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

Found it, we just reached out! Sorry, got lost in the pile :( :( :(

item.description: Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · post Up by 530 AM. Mostly empty streets and coffee at 6 AM. Short walk on the beach until 630. Laptop open and committing by 645 AM. I love my mornings. Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply Here's my general daily schedule, for people who a...
item.content:encoded:
Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · post

Up by 530 AM. Mostly empty streets and coffee at 6 AM. Short walk on the beach until 630. Laptop open and committing by 645 AM. I love my mornings.

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

Here's my general daily schedule, for people who asked:


- 530 awake

- 600 coffee outside w/ wife (or walk), talk

- 630 laptop opening, emails

- 645 OSS triage, try to get a merge in

- 730 wake up daughter, eat breakfast

- 800 work begins

- 1330 break time (gym, games, resting, whatever)

- 1530 wake up daughter (nap)

- 1530 - 1930 family time

- 1930 daughter goes to bed

- 1930 - 2130 family time w/ wife

- 2130 sleep


Obviously things shift all the time, but this is the rough outline of what my everyday looks like.

Tyler Angert (@tylerangert) · context

have you always been a morning person or have kids shifted you that way?

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

Kids shifted me.

item.description: Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · post I’ve been asked for an updated daily schedule given Superlogical, second kid, and AI usage. Here you go: - 530 awake, 20 minute interval cardio - 600 review nightly agents, start new - 700 wake and feed newborn - 730 wake, dress toddler -...
item.content:encoded:
Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · post

I’ve been asked for an updated daily schedule given Superlogical, second kid, and AI usage. Here you go:


- 530 awake, 20 minute interval cardio

- 600 review nightly agents, start new

- 700 wake and feed newborn

- 730 wake, dress toddler

- 745 breakfast with family

- 800 off to work

- 1200 lunch (often with wife)

- 1530 to 1945 family time

- 2000 hang with wife, start new nightly agents


Early 2026 I mentioned a goal of “always have an agent running” but admitted I was realistically only getting agents for a couple hours off work.


As of today, I’ve gotten a LOT better, I regularly have at least 2 agents running constantly with many running through most of the night. I’ll cover this in more detail another time!

Richard Hwang (@rhwang201) · context

This is great, you've inspired me to block off more dedicated time with my newborn. I'd love to have agents running constantly, but I struggle not being in the loop, maybe because I'm mostly doing product dev or maybe skill issue. Looking forward to more details there.

Richard Hwang (@rhwang201) · context

Also: I'm usually very in-the-loop at my desk, and I work until I really need a break. So I find midday/late evening, I'm not sharp enough to deliver a strong spec for long tasks.


Again, maybe skill issue, and I should leave more in the tank to send off those long running tasks?

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

Yes, I had to change my schedule so that I ended my in-the-loop day ~30 minutes earlier so I can spend the last 30 minutes just working on prompts for my nightly tasks.


Note it took me some time to build out those agents, since they're agents in a loop so that they can remain running longer.

katnoria (@katnoria1) · context

Time is the ultimate currency and you seem to be spending it very well.


With the above schedule, you don’t fly to SF anymore? Or is it once a week?

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

Once every couple months and obv those days this schedule doesn’t happen except the wake up the kids and breakfast part

Abinash (@implabinash) · context

I'm really interested in knowing what your schedule looked like when you were actively building Hashicorp during seed or series A, or even later stages?

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

Basically work 16 to 18 hours per day. It wasn’t efficient. It was brute force. I feel I’m able to do the same or more work today in the hours I posted. Experience and tooling.

Axat (@axat_div) · context

Thanks for sharing. As someone that just had a kid, I'm wondering if you outsource any stuff like childcare, cooking, etc. to nannies, chefs, etc. to get some time back? Or do you and your spouse manage all of it?

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

Yes:

- Newborn has a nanny from 8 AM to 330 PM.

- We have a full time housekeeper that does all cleaning, dishes, laundry, car washes, etc. Leaves at 3 PM.

- We have 7 PM to 7 AM night nurses for the new born for now (until they sleep through the night, roughly 4 to 6 months)

- We do most of our own cooking. Parents help some meals (not regularly scheduled, just spontaneously). We have a chef come one night per week for dinner.


The goal with all this is that 330 PM to ~bedtime is private family time. Mornings the kids are usually out anyways.

Adam Bossy (@abossy) · context

What's the rationale of having a chef for one meal per week?

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

A nice break. Diverse food. He meal preps a couple days of lunch too.

Kirk Marple (@kirkmarple) · context

WFH or fighting LA traffic too?

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

2 minute commute (could probably walk lol). Bought a house and converted it into a home office a few blocks over.

Drew Bailey (@_drewbailey) · context

How does your toddler sleep until 730

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

I'm sorry to you to say that she actually sleeps 8 PM to 730 AM and she's 3yo. lol.

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

She also still naps 2.5 hours.

Drew Bailey (@_drewbailey) · context


Drew Bailey (@_drewbailey) · context

Over here with 6am wake ups

Jordan Shurmer (@jshurmer) · context

Well he has night nanny that stays until 7am

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

Just for the newborn until they sleep through the night. Took my first 4 months. My second is currently 3 months old and close (sleeps a consistent 9 hours)

Sam Rose (@samwhoo) · context

Bro you wake your kids what am I reading

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

Got lucky with the sleep and eat lottery. Got unlucky with the insane tantrum lottery relative to our parent friends

Ruslan (@ianberdin) · context

How many days in month you follow this realistically?

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

20?

Filip Mares (@filipmares) · context

When do you sleep?

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

Around 9 to 930 PM

Denis (@denis_eto_ya) · context

do you get distracted by youtube (shorts), x, etc? How do you maintain your focus?

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

No, deleted the apps and/or use parental controls on myself.

abdul (@nerdyprogramme2) · context

do you do any strength training exercises? lifting weights, calisthetics?

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

Lifting twice per week at 2 PM to 3 PM

George Mayer (@georgemayer) · context

when do you fall asleep tho

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

9 to 930.

item.content:encoded:
Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · post

I live in a nice neighborhood. I will never understand how people that are so well off can be so cheap and mean to household employees. Especially those taking care of your kids and being in your house! Take care of people, folks.


One of my neighbors called me a communist in the street because I said I provide healthcare and pay taxes (you know, don’t pay under the table).


I took it as a compliment.

dax (@thdxr) · context

it's crazy my wife is in a chat with other people in the neighborhood and they have insane relationships with their nanny


it's hyper optimized to extract every dollar they can save (meaningless amounts to them)


why would you want to have such a strained relationship with people watching your children

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

same, hard same, i get a ton of dirt from my wife in similar group chats/communities.

Scott (@literalblocks) · context

Any tips on how to find a good nanny?

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

Use an agency that has a high minimum hourly cost (for the hired employee). The quality/education/experience difference between a $25/hour, $35/hour, $50/hour, and $60/hour nanny is MASSIVE.

Dan Goldin (@dangoldin) · context

Earned vs inherited wealth?

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

My actual suspicion is more people living above their means and misallocating assets.

Tim Armandpour (@timarmandpour) · context

I can think of a handful of peeps in our neighborhood that would say something as asinine as that.

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

You still in the same city as me? Lmao

Darragh Grealish (@grealish) · context

Poor kids, they are probably lucky to have a nanny to shield them from such dramas,

I've never tired that Nanny/home care setup,.just reduced my working days for a period of time. It's too expensive child care in Switzerland

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

They don't. This same parent had her kid expelled from a school for being a bully and its not surprising given the upbringing.

item.content:encoded:
Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · post

I’ve been asked for an updated daily schedule given Superlogical, second kid, and AI usage. Here you go:


- 530 awake, 20 minute interval cardio

- 600 review nightly agents, start new

- 700 wake and feed newborn

- 730 wake, dress toddler

- 745 breakfast with family

- 800 off to work

- 1200 lunch (often with wife)

- 1530 to 1945 family time

- 2000 hang with wife, start new nightly agents


Early 2026 I mentioned a goal of “always have an agent running” but admitted I was realistically only getting agents for a couple hours off work.


As of today, I’ve gotten a LOT better, I regularly have at least 2 agents running constantly with many running through most of the night. I’ll cover this in more detail another time!

Filip Mares (@filipmares) · context

When do you sleep?

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

Around 9 to 930 PM

Denis (@denis_eto_ya) · context

do you get distracted by youtube (shorts), x, etc? How do you maintain your focus?

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

No, deleted the apps and/or use parental controls on myself.

abdul (@nerdyprogramme2) · context

do you do any strength training exercises? lifting weights, calisthetics?

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

Lifting twice per week at 2 PM to 3 PM

when do you fall asleep tho

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

9 to 930.

Drew Bailey (@_drewbailey) · context

How does your toddler sleep until 730

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

I'm sorry to you to say that she actually sleeps 8 PM to 730 AM and she's 3yo. lol.

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

She also still naps 2.5 hours.

Kirill Chernakov (@kiryous) · context

God, with this formatting looks like a centuries speedrunning

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

Sorry, how I'm used to seeing things as a pilot, although the single digit hours usually have a `0` in front of it.

Aleks Kin (@thealekskin) · context

How do you manage to have it running all night or near that? Is it some kinda self-feeding loop with the final goal?

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

Yes to the latter.

faizan khan (@faizan10114) · context

when you run night-agents, what are they running on? which agents?

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

A mix:

- Research

- Trial and error solving a fairly open ended task

- Email triage and planning (no writing or sending)

- Issue triage and bug fixing (no auto-push, but code writing, staged for review)

- Judging the work I did the previous day, adversarial review

Tanvir Raj (@tanvirraj) · context

Hey Mitchell, thanks for writing this!

Ive also 2 child


I’m really curious to know more about how you write your prompts for the nightly agents and what kind of work they do .

In my experience most agent tasks not tend to be pretty long may be one hour to 2/3 hours.

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

A mix:

- Research

- Trial and error solving a fairly open ended task

- Email triage and planning (no writing or sending)

- Issue triage and bug fixing (no auto-push, but code writing, staged for review)

- Judging the work I did the previous day, adversarial review

how are you people reviewing code of these “many” agents?

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

Pretty much all I do.

Liz Hurder (@valleyfaraday) · context

the only thing unreasonable about this schedule is waking up the newborn at 7am.


(mine was ready to rage at 6am)

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

So far we've produced two good sleepers. Crossing fingers as the newborn continues to grow. Toddler is a rock star.

Axat (@axat_div) · context

Thanks for sharing. As someone that just had a kid, I'm wondering if you outsource any stuff like childcare, cooking, etc. to nannies, chefs, etc. to get some time back? Or do you and your spouse manage all of it?

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

Yes:

- Newborn has a nanny from 8 AM to 330 PM.

- We have a full time housekeeper that does all cleaning, dishes, laundry, car washes, etc. Leaves at 3 PM.

- We have 7 PM to 7 AM night nurses for the new born for now (until they sleep through the night, roughly 4 to 6 months)

- We do most of our own cooking. Parents help some meals (not regularly scheduled, just spontaneously). We have a chef come one night per week for dinner.


The goal with all this is that 330 PM to ~bedtime is private family time. Mornings the kids are usually out anyways.

in general what do you have your agents do?

A mix:

- Research

- Issue triage and bug fixing (no auto-push, but code writing, staged for review)

- Judging the work I did the previous day, adversarial review

I just do 30 seconds on, 30 seconds off stationary bike sprints (with a short warmup/cooldown). First thing in the morning. Drink a full bottle of water before breakfast. I lift twice a week otherwise.

How do you manage social events with such an early schedule? Take the hit on sleep when you go out?

I don’t go out. I have no interest, I derive no personal joy from it. Of course on the rare occasion for an obligation like birthday or whatever sure. For the most part we see adult friends with kids on the weekends or afternoons.

item.title: Mitchell Hashimoto reply: All http/https is trusted since the preview is visible and browsers have their own security barri...
item.author: Mitchell Hashimoto
item.description: Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · post OSC8 is the terminal sequence for linking arbitrary text (similar to `a` tags in HTML). It is mandatory for a modern terminal experience but prone to malicious use. The next version of Ghostty contains the strongest protections for malici...
item.content:encoded:
Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · post

OSC8 is the terminal sequence for linking arbitrary text (similar to `a` tags in HTML). It is mandatory for a modern terminal experience but prone to malicious use. The next version of Ghostty contains the strongest protections for malicious OSC8 short of disabling it entirely.


In the next version of Ghostty, we've added a classifier for OSC8 URLs (any hidden URL, really) that classifies a URL as: trusted, requires-confirmation, or deny. The screenshots below show the separate requires-confirmation and deny alerts.


We also now show hidden characters in the URL preview in the bottom of the window (previously we interpreted the Unicode directly which allowed maliciously crafted URLs to hide themselves). Hidden characters immediately trigger the `deny` classification, too.


These are the strongest, most comprehensive protections for OSC8 across terminals. As a comparison:


* Alacritty, Kitty, iTerm2, WezTerm: enabled by default with zero filtering at all. Can directly open executables or maliciously crafted schemes without any filter. Can hide the real URL through Unicode tricks.


* Gnome Terminal: enables all OSC8, no configuration I could find to disable. Only rejects remote-host `file://` URLs. No other sanitization, confirmation, etc.


* VS Code Terminal: Allowlist of safe protocols, prompts for unknown, silently replaces whitespace characters. Very good!


* Windows Terminal: Allowlist, prompts for anything executable, prompts for any custom schemes. Very good!

Olivier Mengué (@omengue) · context

I can't even imagine what URL could be marked as trusted except purely ASCII and exactly the same as the displayed text.

Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) · reply

All http/https is trusted since the preview is visible and browsers have their own security barriers. Local files are trusted if they're non-executable and readable and advertise a text format. etc.

- 600 coffee outside w/ wife (or walk), talk

- 630 laptop opening, emails

- 645 OSS triage, try to get a merge in

- 730 wake up daughter, eat breakfast

- 800 work begins

- 1330 break time (gym, games, resting, whatever)

- 1530 wake up daughter (nap)

- 1530 - 1930 family time

- 1930 daughter goes to bed

- 1930 - 2130 family time w/ wife

- 2130 sleep


Obviously things shift all the time, but this is the rough outline of what my everyday looks like.
